{{short description|Mathematician}}

'''Dan Romik''' ([[Hebrew language|Hebrew]]: דן רומיק) is a [[mathematician]] and a professor of mathematics at the [[University of California, Davis]].<ref name="profile">UC Davis Mathematics, [https://www.math.ucdavis.edu/people/general-profile?fac_id=romik Dan Romik].</ref> He is known for contributions to probability theory and discrete mathematics. 

==Biography and Career==
Romik received his Ph.D. from [[Tel Aviv University]] in 2002 under the supervision of David Gilat.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=103099}}.</ref> He has worked at the University of California, Davis since 2009. He is an author of 3 books and over 40 papers, including publications in the [[Annals of Mathematics]] and in the [[Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="zbmathpubs">ZbMath Open, [https://zbmath.org/authors/romik.dan Dan Romik].</ref><ref name="publications">Dan Romik, [https://www.math.ucdavis.edu/~romik/publications/ Publications].</ref> In 2010 he was awarded a [[National Science Foundation CAREER Award]],<ref name="ucdavisnews">UC Davis News, [https://www.ucdavis.edu/news/laurels-mathematician-romik-receives-early-career-grant LAURELS: Mathematician Romik receives early-career grant]</ref> and he was a Simons Fellow in 2012.<ref name="simonsfellow">{{Cite web|url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/grant/simons-fellows-in-mathematics/|title=Simons Fellows in Mathematics|date=June 20, 2012|website=Simons Foundation}}</ref> From 2014 to 2017 he was the chair of the Mathematics Department of the University of California, Davis.<ref name="newsletter">UC Davis Mathematics, [https://www.math.ucdavis.edu/application/files/9716/0996/2691/2017.pdf Mathematics Newsletter - Featuring the 2016-17 Academic Year].</ref>

Much of Romik's work is in the areas of algebraic and enumerative combinatorics. He was an invited speaker at the [[FPSAC]] 2017 and [[AofA—International Meeting on Combinatorial, Probabilistic, and Asymptotic Methods in the Analysis of Algorithms|AofA]] 2017 conferences and served as co-chair of the FPSAC 2021 program committee.<ref name="fpsac2017">{{Cite web|url=https://fpsac.org/invited_speakers/|title=All time invited speakers · FPSAC / SFCA|website=fpsac.org}}</ref><ref name="aofa2017">{{Cite web|url=https://aofa2017.cs.princeton.edu/speakers/|title=Invited Speakers · AofA2017|website=aofa2017.cs.princeton.edu}}</ref><ref name="fpsac2021">{{Cite web|url=https://fpsac.org/confs/fpsac-2021/|title=Fpsac 2021 · FPSAC / SFCA|website=fpsac.org}}</ref>

==Work==

===The sphere packing problem===
In 2023, Romik published a paper simplifying [[Maryna Viazovska]]'s solution to the [[sphere packing problem]] in dimension 8. Viazovska's original solution relied on computer calculations to verify analytical inequalities that were an essential ingredient in her proof, making the proof a [[computer-assisted proof]]. Romik's paper presents a proof of the same inequalities that does not rely on computer calculations.<ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Romik | first1=Dan
| title=On Viazovska's modular form inequalities
| journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
| date=2023
| volume=120
| issue=43
| article-number=e2304891120
| doi=10.1073/pnas.2304891120 | doi-access=free
| pmid=37851677
| pmc=10614599
| arxiv=2303.13427| s2cid=257687204}}</ref>

===The moving sofa problem===
Romik's research work on the [[moving sofa problem]] has been featured on the [[Numberphile]] educational YouTube channel,<ref name="numberphile">Numberphile, [https://www.numberphile.com/videos/the-moving-sofa-problem The Moving Sofa Problem].</ref> in an article in [[Popular Mechanics]],<ref name="popularmech">Popular Mechanics, [https://www.popularmechanics.com/science/math/a25808/moving-sofa-problem/ Why Mathematicians Cannot Solve the Problem of Moving Your Sofa]</ref> and in several other news publications and websites.<ref name="amsblog">Visual Insight, American Mathematical Society Blogs, [https://blogs.ams.org/visualinsight/2016/12/15/romiks-ambidextrous-sofa/ Romik's Ambidextrous Sofa]</ref><ref name="physorg">Phys.org, [https://phys.org/news/2017-03-sofa-problem-stumped-mathematicians-furniture.html New twist on sofa problem that stumped mathematicians and furniture movers]</ref><ref name="express">The Daily Express, [https://www.express.co.uk/news/uk/1493103/maths-whizz-mathematicians-move-sofa-new-home Moving a sofa into a house is so tricky - it's stumped mathematicians for years]</ref><ref name="3dprint">3DPrint.com, [https://3dprint.com/168718/moving-sofa-problem-3d-printing/ UC Davis Mathematician Uses 3D Printing to Deliver New Insight into Moving Sofa Problem]</ref><ref name="3quarks">3 Quarks Daily, [https://3quarksdaily.com/3quarksdaily/2020/11/moving-sofas-in-the-apocalypse.html Moving Sofas in the Apocalypse]</ref><ref name="econometrist">De Econometrist, [https://www.deeconometrist.nl/mathematics/the-worlds-easiest-unsolvable-problem/ The Moving Sofa Problem]</ref><ref name="openmind">OpenMind, [https://www.bbvaopenmind.com/en/about-us/ Once Upon a Time, a Sofa in a Hallway…]</ref>

===Software===
Romik developed several software packages accompanying his research articles.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dan Romik's home page - Software|access-date=October 23, 2023|url=https://www.math.ucdavis.edu/~romik/software/}}</ref> He is the creator of the MadHat software system for mathematical typesetting and publishing.<ref name="madhat">[https://madhat.design/about/ MadHat - About].</ref>
